- `galaxy-sports-edge-research-audit.md` ("Galaxy Sports Edge Research Audit"): research corpus triage (1,300+ arXiv rows, 7 clusters) + honest GSE system audit (launch readiness 29.00/100; inverted confidence Brier 0.3617, z=−10.7, n=2,385; CLV 40.8% decided-only vs 52.4% floor; closing-line CRPS 7.109 beats all internal models). Top transfers: (1) train probability heads under Brier loss not BCE (cited NCAA LSTM+Brier 0.159 vs Transformer+BCE best AUC 0.847, worse calibration); (2) strict decoupling: play-by-play-only performance engine vs market pricing engine, dual CLV reporting (23.2% system / 40.8% decided); (3) sort/display on devigged marketFairProb until the model beats the close, purge inverted single-point confidence. Operational states in the doc (PR #866/#867/#868, CI #2948, board gate 2026-09-24) are snapshots as of 2026-09-19/21 — re-verify against the live repo.
- `conformal-prediction-small-sample-calibration-audit.md` ("Auditing Conformal Prediction, Small-Sample Calibration, and Sports Market Probabilities for GSE"): theoretical backbone for the calibration/UQ posture — exact finite-sample formulas (CQR, Jackknife+, Venn-Abers), fail-closed scarce-data policy, gates (ECE ≤ 0.05, Venn-Abers width ≤ 0.20, n ≥ 9 for 90% CQR). FLAG: GSE's own `cqr.ts` (`apps/web/lib/calibration/conformalQuantile`) contains the exact small-sample clamp the doc bans — clamps rank to n−1 instead of returning +∞/refusal when n<9 at α=0.1, falsely certifying 90% coverage while delivering 83.33% (6.67pp fake tightness). Fix: return +∞ + machine-readable No-Bet signal; `cqr.test.ts` encodes the wrong behavior. Top transfers: (1) that fix; (2) Venn-Abers [p₀,p₁] for moneylines with p₁−p₀>0.20 → refuse; (3) CLV discipline + fail-closed No-Bet for props with n<9 (Jackknife+ substitute).
- `architectural-blueprint-calibrated-tracking-decoupled-engine.md` ("Architectural Blueprint for a Calibrated, Tracking-Decoupled Sports Probability Engine"): architecture SPEC, not an empirical paper — zero backtests; all gates (0.01/150, Δp>0.20, 200–400 ms) are asserted starting priors. Top transfers: (1) CRPS + Gaussian margin densities as primary scoring rule for spreads/totals (closed form via Φ/φ) with ≥150-settled / 0.01-improvement promotion gate (feeds PR #96 leaderboard); (2) conformal honesty package: ban clamped CQR (fail-closed No-Bet), Jackknife+ at true 1−2α for NFL-scale n≈70, Venn-Abers epistemic intervals; (3) Shin devigging (quadratic solve for insider z) replacing proportional normalization everywhere implied probabilities feed edge claims. Needs reconciliation with the conformal audit + CQR research before coding.
- `world-class-sports-probability-engine-corpus-audit.md` ("World-Class Sports Probability Engine Corpus Audit"): architecture doctrine paper — high calibration value, zero novel empirical results; 22 equation images recovered from docx PNGs. Top transfers: (1) ban quantile clamping + fail-closed conformal policy (n=5/α=0.10 worked example: k=6>n → +∞; clamping claims 90%, delivers 83.33%); (2) Venn-Abers multiprobability bounds for moneylines; (3) decouple performance from market pricing + prove edge with the Forecast-Skill E-process (anytime-valid edge statistic vs fixed-n p-values; validates shadow pipeline design). Navier-Stokes/AGI-swarm material is unverifiable vision — treat as such.
- `cqr-research.md` ("CQR Research"): full survey of Conformalized Quantile Regression 2019–2026 (exact CQR formulas, jackknife+ 1−2α guarantee, missing-data/conditional-coverage/time-series extensions); numerical results sparse (abstract-fragment level) so value is methodological. Top transfers: (1) CQR intervals on EVERY pick: quantile regressors at α/2 and 1−α/2, conformal-calibrate E_i=max{q̂_lo−Y_i, Y_i−q̂_hi}, publish C(x)=[q̂_lo−Q̂, q̂_hi+Q̂] — finite-sample P(Y∈C(X))≥1−α, monetizable as "90% edge bands" on cards/DFS packet; (2) rolling-origin/KOWCPI calibration for weekly NFL data (naive split CP decays as the calibration set goes stale — kernel-weight recent observations instead); (3) impute-then-predict+conformalize for injury-lineup uncertainty (Zaffran et al. marginal-validity theorem incl. MNAR under exchangeability+symmetric imputation), with mask-conditional coverage caveat logged as known risk.

### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)
- @sfdata9ers "Post-Game Win Expectancy" (PGWE): "How likely is each team to win if the game were replayed with the same key stats?" — a replay-simulation-style upset detector; 4 PGWE upsets in Week 2 (TEN 92.4% lost to PHI; HOU 79.1% lost to CIN; NYJ won vs GB 63.5%; BAL 60.1% lost to NO). Callout box: "PGWE UNDER-DOG WON THE GAME".
- @hawkblogger snap-for-snap on/off split: charted individual blocking metrics (Sumer) + team on/off splits (EPA, success, yardage via nflverse) — the twist is the divergence: "Haynes won every blocking measure. The team splits went the other way."
- @GetProblay reply on the SumerSports RB chart: "Same rushing total, different process. Cook is getting far more before contact; Walker is creating far more afterward. Raw yards per carry hides that difference. Blocking environment and runner-created yardage aren't interchangeable."
- SūmerPass newly exposed "rushing yards before contact" (YBC) as a queryable column at team + individual RB/QB level.
- FantasyPtsData's complementary "Catchable Air Yards" / "Uncatchable Air Yards" and rate versions (catchable target rate, catchable air-yardage rate) — proprietary charted pair appearing across @FantasyPtsData, @ScottBarrettDFB, @KyleM_FF today.
- statyx.io's "Target Area Matchup" board (field-zone grid with Tough/Soft matchup ranks + NQ flag) and "Throw distribution by depth and lane" board; the latter explicitly displays accuracy as CPOE "because completion rate alone is not comparable between a screen and a 25-yard throw."
- @Shauncore / FantasyPtsData "Blitz Rate & Under-Pressure Rate" 2×2 quadrant framing with qualitative labels ("Pressure without blitzing", "Blitzing and getting home", "Try something else", "Blitzing and not getting home").
- @benbbaldwin's Remaining SOS with stated definition (average remaining opponent win% vs. league-average team on neutral field, site-adjusted), from odds-derived team-strength ratings.
- @DynatyzeFF "SEPARATION × TPRR": novel combination of TPRR with average separation created as a quadrant scatter from their own NFL Tape product.
- @TheCurrentTalk "Weighted EPA (WEPA)/play": a "Team Tiers" tool offers an EPA vs Weighted EPA toggle for team offense/defense scatter; no weighting definition given; tool site URL not identified.
- @AcccountStat three-source averaging: YAC per rush × avoided tackles per rush averaged across NFL Pro, PFF, and SumerSports — a multi-source composite with min-15-attempts filter.
- @NFL_University Deep Pass % + Deep Pass EPA paired leaderboard: volume rate and efficiency combined in one Week-2 cut (e.g. Mayfield 26.5% deep pass rate but −1.8 Deep Pass EPA; Young 19.4% / +11.4).

### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)
- @MagicSportsGuy "Cardio Index": cross of Route Participation % against TPRR to flag pass catchers running a high route share with a low target rate; author frames the positive-regression read (high route % tends to pull targets upward, with a "sacrificial role" caveat). Proprietary @StatRankings; full stat page announced for statrankings.com.
- @SamHoppen "Week 3 NFL Composite Power Ratings": mean-of-6 composite (FPI, nfelo, Inpredictable, Unexpected Points, FTN DVOA, PFF) expressed as expected spread vs an average team, with per-team std dev across sources as a disagreement gauge (high: CHI 2.3, NYG 2.4; low: BAL 0.4, LV 0.5). Different composite construction than @benbbaldwin's market-implied ratings (AM): model-mean vs prediction-market blend.
- @SumerSports "Stacking the box doesn't stop the run" thread (4:36 PM CDT, https://x.com/SumerSports/status/2102512386884477357): box-count-vs-rush-success scatterplot framing — average defenders in the box (x) vs rushing success rate allowed (y), success axis INVERTED so up-and-right is better, league-average reference lines, footer "NFL · 2026 regular season, Weeks 1-2 · designed runs · success axis inverted, so up and right is better" / "Data & Figure: @SumerSports". Thread layers: "Every team's run concept mix" (image) and "Buffalo's backs get the most room: yards before contact per designed carry, top 5 and bottom 5 of 32" with the attributed claim that the Bills, Rams and Broncos — "all man/gap-heavy teams" — are the only teams averaging over 2 yards before contact on designed runs. Reply-thread caveat (attributed to PressX_Global): box counts aren't random — defenses stack against teams they already expect to run (selection bias).

- @statyxio, 2026-09-23 6:20 PM CDT — "WEEK 2: IT WASN'T JUST ABOUT VOLUME" (new composite narrative: intended air-yard share + aIAY + RYOE). Post text (verbatim): "Week 2 showed that volume isn't always the biggest change. 👀 Sometimes the workload barely moves. What changes is what teams get out of it. CeeDee Lamb didn't need more targets. He got better ones. He went 8 → 9 targets, but his intended-air-yard share jumped 35.9% → 57.4%. aIAY went 11.5 → 16.2. The result? 44 → 153 receiving yards. Davante Adams saw a similar shift in LA. His targets moved 6 → 10, but his intended-air-yard share exploded 27.2% → 57.4% and aIAY went 10.8 → 18.3. The Rams also jumped from 321 → 481 total yards. Kyren Williams barely saw his workload change. His efficiency did. 11 → 12 carries. Expected rushing yards stayed almost identical at 48.8 → 50.9, but actual production jumped 41 → 85 yards, resulting in +34.1 RYOE. And the interesting part? 🛡️ New England is showing a different kind of efficiency. Through two games, the Patriots have allowed just [truncated in display]". Definitions (author's words): intended air-yard share (air-yard share), aIAY (average intended air yards), RYOE (run yards over expectation) vs expected rushing yards. ### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)
- @PFF "QB ACCURACY INDEX" (new launch): ball-placement charting (ACC% / PLUS% / CAT INAC% / UNC INAC% / OTHER) combined with CPOE and ACCOE (accuracy over expectation on charted placement rather than completions) plus AJ% in one per-QB report — the first public-facing composite of PFF's accuracy charting tiers with expectation-adjusted measures. Thread caveats (attributed): Allen 2nd in CPOE (+14.3) but only 15th in accurate throws (61.5%) — "completes way more than he should because of what happens after the catch"; questions about throw-difficulty accounting and tight-coverage placement being dinged.
- @SumerSports "Impact Play": "When a player meaningfully outperforms expectations for their role, the play is surfaced as an Impact Play" — a new proprietary outcome-vs-expectation role model; Dexter Lawrence leads all interior DL in impact plays and is tied for the league lead among all defensive players. Different frame from the same thread as the box-count discussion.
- @PattonAnalytics "Play Caller Tendencies": Y-Aware PCA blending personnel diversification, play sequencing, and other play-caller process metrics into one Tendency Rating (Shanahan top, Bobby Slowik bottom); author working through kinks on the defensive version. Thread critique (attributed): "Seems like a pretty vague stat. Tendency to what exactly?"

- @sfdata9ers drops-EPA-lost × penalty-EPA-gained player combo (Dak Prescott: −9.4 on drops, +7.7 on penalties) — a new two-metric offset framing.
- @MagicSportsGuy ARBY methodology now explicit: 65% ARBY / 35% RB YPC per side, offense/defense 50/50, game-weighted 5/2 across the 2025 Wk 13-17 + 2026 Wk 1-2 windows; TNF grades ATL 61 vs GB 58. Public ARBY stat pages linked for the first time.

## ENGINE BENCHMARK: TIMESFM-3 FOUNDATION FORECASTER (2026-09-24, Motif)

**Source:** IG save @voxaris_ai 2026-09-01 (verified release facts via web 2026-09-24); the v1 paper already has a deep ledger (`docs/research/2026-09-21/arxiv-deep/2122-timesfm-decoder-only-foundation-model.md`).

**Metric/tool:** Google TimesFM-3 (released 2026-08-31): 330M-param time-series foundation model, `google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch` on HF. Multivariate natively, past-only + past/future covariates, 9 quantile heads (q10–q90), non-autoregressive single-pass decode. `pip install timesfm[torch]`; darts PR #3199 ports it; MLX port + MCP wrapper exist.

**Engine gap:** no pretrained time-series backbone anywhere in the engine or corpus (confirmed by repo grep 2026-09-21). Fits two lanes: (a) research-loop baseline for time-series sub-tasks (line movement, totals drift) — never the pick path; (b) covariate experiments for the thin weather lane (wave-3 arXiv). 9-quantile output is a ready-made uncertainty source to compare against Mimo's conformal calibration.

**LICENSE GATE:** weights are **non-commercial, non-production** (TimesFM Non-Commercial License v1.0, verified 2026-09-24 on the official HF card). Eval/research/internal use only. Cannot generate picks, sit behind a paid API, or touch `generate-signal-slate.ts` / the book path. Commercial path = BigQuery `AI.FORECAST`. (Repo is not gated — no terms click needed.)

**LIVE:** prereg #1 ran 2026-09-24 on HF Space `Beexly/timesfm3-benchmark` (Docker; weights baked at build on HF's network; serves aggregate results only) — **verdict MET**: TimesFM median MAE 0.2433 vs naive 0.7505 (ratio 0.324 ≤ 0.80). Run record: `docs/research/2026-09-24/evals/timesfm3-space/SPACE.md`; numbers in `docs/research/2026-09-24/evals/prereg-timesfm3-mechanics.md`. Mechanics validated; sports-skill NOT claimed — benchmark #2 needs its own prereg.

- @hawkblogger, 2026-09-25 5:58 PM CDT — "Top 20 Run Blocking OL (T, G, C) Through Week 2". Metric: "Run block grade" = "Disruption rate grade". Author methodology (verbatim): "Sumer Sports charts every run play by player: which blockers each defender faced, on every snap. A blocker's grade is how much he moves the disruption rate on a typical rep, compared with an average blocker facing the same defenders. Lower is better, so the best grades are negative. Bars always point right for a good grade. Every rep counts who was across from him. Winning against a top defender counts for more than winning against a backup, and every defender's own grade is worked out at the same time. Double teams are handled on their own, so a player who draws extra blockers is not marked down for it. Players with few reps are pulled toward average until the sample earns a strong grade. Games used: Blended = 2026 through Week 3, with 2025 counted at 50% and fading out by Week 6. Trend compares this season with his own past: his reps this year against what his earlier grade predicted against the same opponents. Over expected is the running total: disruptions above or below what an average blocker would have had against the same opponents." ### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)

- **@hawkblogger "HB Analytics" composite family — genuine new metric product (strongest innovation kernel of the day).** Opponent-adjusted, double-team-aware, Bayesian-shrunk, time-blended grades: run blockers graded by "disruption rate grade" (how much a blocker moves the disruption rate vs an average blocker facing the same defenders; defender quality solved simultaneously; double teams handled separately; low-rep players pulled toward average; blended 2026-through-Week-3 with 2025 at 50% fading by Week 6); coverage defenders graded by "yards per route grade" (same simultaneous-solution framing for receivers faced; brackets/help handled separately). Both shipped with trend-vs-past and "over expected" running totals. Data: Sumer Sports play-by-player charting; published at stats.hawkblogger.com under the "HB ANALYTICS" brand. Three posts (run block OL, cover safeties, cover corners) — same metric engine, different position filters.
- @sfdata9ers "Offensive Red Zone Efficiency" — composite decomposition: points per RZ trip split into TD%/FG%/Scored% in one table (attributed as a framing twist, not a new metric).
- Different-angle (attributed): @GridironInfo_ continues his Next Gen Stats QB leaderboard series — time-to-throw (9/25 AM) → worst aDOT → success rate → worst EPA/dropback (9/25 PM); same source (nflreadpy/Next Gen Stats), different metric each post. @FantasyPtsData Pitts splits = TPRR conditioned on teammate presence on/off the field (a notable framing of a known metric; compare 9/24 @BeyondTheADP TPRR deep dive). @ffdataroma Concepcion splits = per-route efficiency conditioned on safety shell. @xEP_Network Purdy = percentile framing of the CPOE + EPA/dropback combo. @sfdata9ers EPA-allowed scatter = defensive EPA split by dropback vs rush (different cut from offensive EPA posts). @sfdata9ers 3rd-and-long = situational quadrant plot (offense vs defense rates). @DevyEusuf 5h ago: "Xavier Worthy 0.57 YPRR on the season" — single-player stat note, no chart; noted only, not inventoried.

### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)

- **@MagicSportsGuy "ARBY" (Adjusted Run Blocking Yards) — genuine named composite metric.** ARBY blends offensive and defensive run-blocking into one RB matchup score with a stated weighting formula (65% prior season / 35% current; 65% ARBY / 35% RB yards per carry; 50/50 offense-defense) — the first explicitly formula-disclosed trench composite in this sweep series; the Week 3 board is framed as the account's "weekly DFS breakdown" of RB/OL matchup data. Data: statrankings.com.
- @GridironInfo_ "WR Avg. Separation" leaderboards (two cuts: league Top 10 + each team's leading receiver) — new NGS-metric cut from the same account's continuing series (time-to-throw → aDOT → success rate → EPA/dropback → aggressiveness → passer rating → separation).
- @FantasyPtsData EPA/Play by personnel grouping — 12-personnel vs "all other" split framed around a player's return (Bowers); a situational personnel-split framing on Fantasy Points Data's EPA tool, with a "5th-worst" claim attached to the comparison column.
- @FantasyPtsData targets/game on behind-LOS throws — a manufactured-target rate split across seasons (2026 vs 2025), teased with eye emojis; a new usage-shape metric on the Fantasy Points Data pipe.
- @PFF drive-TD-rate floor — "% of offensive drives ending in a TD" as a team inefficiency leaderboard; the pass-rush-win-rate post is a straight team leaderboard of PFF's win-rate stat with fan/beat-writer derivatives spreading within hours.

## FILM-PIPELINE PATENT PROGRAM (2026-09-29, Motif — RESEARCH ONLY, not approved for build)

Automated broadcast-film pipeline from expired-patent architectures, re-implemented with modern tools: ingest broadcast → play segmentation → replay discrimination → camera calibration → field-anchored telestration → semantic moment search. Outputs (both internal-only per the public/private doctrine): (a) 2–4s telestrated clips for the X video operation; (b) automated charting labels → proprietary training data (variance model, signals table, rankings). The labeled dataset builds itself as a byproduct of the content pipeline.

**Patent numbers (all at `https://patents.google.com/patent/<NUMBER>/en`):**
- Telestration (Sportvision lineage): US7075556B1, US5953077A, US6133946A, US6292130B1, US6229550B1, US6466275B1
- Summarization (Sharp Labs): US7499077B2, US7312812B2, US7639275B2, US7474331B2, US8018491B2
- Replay ID: US7474698B2, US7653131B2
- Vanishing-point: US7609855B2 (granted; filed as US20060132487A1)

**Why they stopped (forensics 2026-09-29):** Sportvision WON — Emmy-winning yellow line, still on NFL broadcasts via SMT (acquired Sportvision Oct 2016); patents aged out by normal 20-year term 2017–2019. Sharp Labs was orphaned (parent wouldn't productize, HiMpact/ESPN spin-out fizzled) + Sharp's 2012–2016 collapse/Foxconn takeover + handcrafted heuristics superseded by learned methods. Neither stopped because the problem was unsolvable. Field has since validated the architecture (nflgsplat on consumer RTX 4080; soccer charting real-time on RTX 4060).

**Two limitations to design around:** (1) calibration/registration fragility → image-based match-moving + neural segmentation, zero stadium hardware; (2) single-cue brittleness → multimodal learned boundaries (OCR/clock, audio, data feeds) with explicit uncertainty, no single broadcast cue as ground truth. Walk-through gaps documented: automatic generation (theirs is operator-triggered), segmentation compositing (theirs is colorimetry), learned boundaries (theirs are handcrafted).

**Preconditions before Phase 0:** (a) footage sourcing resolved — input broadcast video must be legitimately obtained; (b) 3-game hand-labeled validation set built. **Kill rule:** any phase missing its gate twice gets redesigned or killed. **Backend:** local RTX 4080-class GPU for prototyping; Neon for metadata/labels/pgvector; object storage for video. **APIs: none required** — broadcast in, clips/labels out. Family/continuation review still owed before any build.

Docs (all under `docs/engine/research/2026-09-29/`): `film-pipeline-implementation-plan-2026-09-29.md` (full plan: scope, cause→action chain, expected results, forecasted discrepancies, data/backend/API needs) · `patent-forensics-2026-09-29.md` (per-patent claims + corporate trails) · `patent-mining-are-gse-2026-09-29.md` (idea report) · `second-pass-leverage-review-2026-09-29.md` (cross-report synthesis) · `second-pass-gap-fills-2026-09-29.md` (5 empirical gap-fills with sources) · `awesome-apps-gse-leverage-map-2026-09-29.md` (45-item leverage map) · `second-pass-raw-synthesis-2026-09-29.md` (raw synthesis notes) · `forensics-evidence-sharp-2026-09-29.md` + `forensics-evidence-sportvision-2026-09-29.md` (raw per-company evidence behind the forensics).

7. @MagicSportsGuy (Kevin Adams; bio: "Founder, @StatRankings & FTN
   Fantasy/Data") — "TNF Matchup Report Steelers vs. Browns"
   (2026-09-30 ~2:09 PM CDT). 3-slide "MagicSportsBreakdown Week 4 · 2026"

   prices: PIT -2.5 (-111), total 38.5). The post quotes his Sep 25 CB/WR
   matchup-data post; the new slides carry the Week 4 report.
   Proprietary metric definitions as stated in the slides:
   - ARBY: "Adjusted Run Blocking Yards (ARBY)".
   - ARBY RB Matchup Grade: "league average 50, Week 4 slate average 51.9.
     Rank is among the 32 Week 4 run matchups. Higher is a better matchup
     for the offense."
   - "RB yards over blocking (RB yards/carry minus team ARBY/carry), 2026".
   - PROE+: "pass rate over expected".
   - Explosive rate: "Offense: share of plays that go for an explosive gain,
     rank by highest, rank by lowest. Home and away are the 2026 splits."
   - Havoc rate: "Share of defensive plays with a tackle for loss, forced
     fumble, pass deflection or interception. Rank by highest; home and away
     are the 2026 splits."
   - First-read target share: "Share of a player's targets that came as the
     quarterback's first read, 2026 Weeks 1-3, minimum 4 targets. Rank in
     parentheses is out of 221 qualifiers."
   - TPRR: "targets per route run against the coverage the defense plays
     more; 2025 shown with that season's team when different."
   - Tgt share: "true target share: the share of team pass attempts
     directed at the player."
   - Corners caption: "2026 Weeks 1-3, listed corners and nickels from the
     depth chart with at least 25 coverage routes. Left and right are the
     share of routes covered on the offense's left or right. Ranks (top 20
     only) are out of 157 qualifying defenders."
   - Goal-line caption: "Backs with at least 6 carries in the red zone or 3
     inside the 5. Share is the back's portion of his team's running-back
     carries in that zone."

### INNOVATION CANDIDATES (attributed; notes, not build orders)

- "Create Rate" (@PattonAnalytics, item 16): outside-pocket plays +
  beyond-first-read attempts, plotted vs EPA/dropback. New composite.
- "Tendency Rating" (@PattonAnalytics, item 18): personnel diversification
  + play sequencing + other tendencies, per play caller. New composite
  (construction unstated — a commenter asked what "+.2" means; no reply).
- MOFC/MOFO EPA-per-dropback split (@PattonAnalytics, item 19):
  coverage-structure split of QB efficiency. Twist on existing metric.
- ARBY / ARBY RB Matchup Grade / PROE+ / Havoc rate (StatRankings via
  @MagicSportsGuy, item 7): Adjusted Run Blocking Yards, matchup grades,
  pass rate over expected, havoc rate (TFL + forced fumble + PD + INT).
  New composite family.
- "Average Separation Score" (SEP SCORE), AYRR, XFP/RR, YPTOE, 1D/RR
  (@FantasyPtsData, items 14-15): new receiver composites (SEP SCORE
  debuted in Data Suite 2.0). AYRR = air yards per route run; XFP/RR =
  expected fantasy points per route run; YPTOE = yards per target over
  expected; 1D/RR = first downs per route run.
- Multi-source Composite Power Ratings (@SamHoppen, item 26): FPI + nfelo
  + Inpredictable + Unexpected Points + FTN DVOA + PFF combined into
  expected spread vs average. New composite.
- IDL pass-rush win rate vs run-defense impact play rate two-way scatter
  (@SamHoppen/Sumer Sports, item 27): combination of two metrics for
  interior DL evaluation.
- "Robbed Score" (@AjayTakes): Route Win Rate + TPRR + uncatchable target
  % — backtest still pending (see below).
- Route IQ man/zone classified splits (@statyxio, item 13): opponent
  man/zone rates from classified Route IQ plays.
- QB Turnover = INT + FUM lost (@GridironInfo_, item 11): simple defined
  composite.

  have been chart-specific to the Aggressiveness post, not a standing
  credit on the account's current chart series.
- @sfdata9ers EPA/half scatter (item 3) is a different angle on the
  account's own prior EPA leaderboards: intra-player half splits with an
  equality diagonal, rather than a ranked leaderboard.
- @hawkblogger's HB Daily posts (items 4-6) are a different angle on
  pressure stats: on/off personnel-package splits and D-line alignment
  conditionals, using Sumer charting as the shared source — the same
  source family cited by @SumerSports' platform pitch in this run.
- @MagicSportsGuy's statrankings methodology page (item 8) is a different
  angle on data sourcing: a public methodology doc stating exactly which
  upstream feeds each layer uses (nflverse pbp, FTN charting/participation/
  snaps, PropLine odds, multi-site ADP) — one of the more transparent
  pipelines among the inventoried independent accounts.

### INNOVATION CANDIDATES

- @GridironInfo_ opponent-outcome series (items 9-11): a three-chart
  family framing defensive performance by drive outcomes — series-end
  distribution, first-down conversion down distribution, drive-end
  distribution — rather than EPA or yards. Treats defensive identity as a
  distribution over terminal events; Minnesota's league-lead repeats
  across all three framings.
- @hawkblogger on/off + alignment-conditional EPA (items 4-5): evaluating
  individual pass-rushers by team pressure/EPA with them in specific
  packages (Fowler 4-man fronts) and by D-line alignment (Williams/Murphy
  inside vs outside). Author's own stated kernel: "noisy on/off splits and
  small sample" — the innovation is the framing (package-conditional
  team performance), not the numbers.
- @MagicSportsGuy coverageIQ+ / WR/CB+ launch (item 8): man-coverage WR
  splits (1st Read Target Share, FPRR, YPRR vs man, min. 25 routes vs
  man) — a new public tool surface at statrankings.com/nfl/wr-cb with
  coverage-shell splits and heat maps; Garrett Wilson 1st in all three
  vs-man metrics.
- @statyxio run-concept usage shares x RYOE/attempt (item 13): pairing
  Inside/Outside/Gap-power shares with rush-yards-over-expected per
  attempt (Ken Walker #1 balanced profile) — run-game style classification
  anchored to an efficiency outcome.
- @sfdata9ers QB EPA/Play per-half scatter (item 3): intra-QB half splits
  with an equality diagonal — a fade/consistency lens (Purdy top-right in
  both halves; Ward last in 1st, Rodgers last in 2nd).
- @TheHallmanAlgo bet-framing (item 21): the TPRR/YPRR/1D-RR usage-
  efficiency trio packaged as a prop-bet signal (DJ Moore over 48.5 rec
  yards), showing how the three efficiency ranks travel together.

### DATA-ACCESS

- statrankings.com (author: @MagicSportsGuy, Founder of @StatRankings &
  FTN Fantasy/Data): "The Ultimate Sports Data Hub" — 675+ advanced NFL
  stats; statsuite+; coverageIQ+ (man/zone splits, all eight coverage
  shells, 132 WR coverage stats); NFL Stats Archive — every published stat
  downloadable as CSV, one file per category per season, zipped, back to
  2021, base & advanced, regular season & playoffs. Methodology page
  (statrankings.com/methodology) states: NFL play-by-play, rosters,
  schedules, injury reports and depth charts from nflverse (nflfastR);
  advanced charting, participation and snap-count data from FTN Data;
  betting odds from PropLine; ADP compiled from Underdog, DraftKings,
  Drafters, Sleeper, Yahoo, ESPN, NFL.
- statyx.io (@statyxio): "NFL Analytics and Player Prop Research Tool" —
  Data Lab (free), Coverage Engine, End Zone Engine, NFL Depth Charts,
  Glossary, API access link (FAQ: "Does Statyx offer widgets or an API
  for businesses?"), 7-day free trial. No third-party data provider stated
  on homepage/FAQ.
- Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0 (data.fantasypoints.com / profile states
  "FantasyPoints.com Data Partner") — @FantasyPtsData's stated analytics
  product; used for the Hurts deep-ball fact-check table.
- Sumer charting (@SumerSports): cited by @hawkblogger ("Sumer charting",
  "Pressure, sacks: Sumer"); pinned post: "A football research platform
  made for diehards, by diehards. Start free: bit.ly/getsumerpass"

- FTN (ftn): cited by @hawkblogger's Rams chart ("DVOA: FTN"); FTN Data

- nflverse: cited by @hawkblogger's Rams chart ("EPA, third downs:

- ko-fi.com/sfdata9ers — donation page only; no data/API documentation.

### INNOVATION NOTES (attributed, not build orders)

- @AjayTakes "Robbed Score": (Route Win Rate − TPRR) + uncatchable
  target % + (XFPTS − FPTS), mapped against Separation Score — a
  buy-low composite framing separation-production divergence. First
  confirmed sighting after six missing sweeps.
- @FantasyPtsData "Most Condensed Offenses by First-Read Target Share":
  team-level concentration metric = No. 1 + No. 2 pass-catchers'
  combined first-read share (Cardinals 70.4%, Lions 62.9%, Giants 62.3%).
- @FantasyPtsData CB separation-at-catch family: STEP+ % / BLANKETED %
  (Sneed 75.8% STEP+, 15.2% BLANKETED vs league avg 63.7%/22.5%).
- @PattonAnalytics EPA-per-completion split into air-yards vs YAC
  components ("congruency" framing; only completions; data @nflreadr).
- @ColeJacksonFB "True pass set pass rush win rate" — named qualifier
  variant of PRWR.
- @MagicSportsGuy StatRankings AI Connector: natural-language query
  ("Saints RB usage in the 4th quarter of week 3") → generated usage
  table — tooling innovation, not a metric.
- @Shauncore built team-level DB positive/negative play rates with the
  SumerSports SumerBrain tool — analyst-built metric on a vendor tool.
- @sfdata9ers Post-Game Win Expectancy (replay-based) + season
  expected-wins tracking (HOU 2.55 expected, 0 actual).
- Keon Coleman YPRR with/without DJ Moore on field (3.70 vs 1.31);
  49ers success rate with/without Juszczyk (56.9% vs 49.7%) —
  teammate/personnel-conditioned splits.
- @GridironInfo_ "passes to or past the sticks" (air yards ≥ yards to
  go) — sticks-relative aggressiveness rate (Allen 51%, league avg 43%).
- @cmain7 game-level PROE usage: Falcons dead last in PROE + 46%
  situation-neutral pass rate + top-5 rushing efficiency — a different
  angle on the already-inventoried PROE.
- @TSeel14 "Win Rate Route Trees" — route-level win rates by route tree
  for team pass-catcher groups.

### REPEAT-ANGLE / INNOVATION KERNELS (attributed notes, not build orders)

- ARBY Matchup Rating as a stated-weight composite: 65% 2025 / 35%
  2026 season blend × 65% ARBY / 35% RB YPC × 50/50 offense-defense —
  proprietary Adjusted Run Blocking Yards fused with YPC and a
  defensive counterpart into one score (@MagicSportsGuy/StatRankings).
- Net lucky wins as a luck derivative: actual wins minus the sum of
  each game's modeled win likelihood, from 160K resimulations of
  "every loose ball, field goal, and dropped pass" (@nfl_simulator).
- "Likely points" success rate twist: success = gaining likely points
  (~45% of plays), and a takeaway counts as a success for the defense
  that made it — points-based success, not yardage-based
  (@nfl_simulator).
- Net-likely-points isolines: diagonal lines joining teams with equal
  net likely points per game across the Net Success Rate vs Net Yards
  Per Play chart (@nfl_simulator).
- Kalshi-derived stacked playoff probabilities as directly
  market-implied ratings: 1-seed/division/wild-card odds per team
  (@GridironInfo_).
- SEP SCORE / SEP MS (@FantasyPtsData, via @DevyEusuf and
  @ScottBarrettDFB): proprietary separation score + a "separation
  market share" share stat; used in SEP SCORE vs YPRR quadrants.
- QBRK (@FantasyPtsData, via @ScottBarrettDFB): proprietary 0-100-ish
  QB rating alongside QBEFF; inputs include BTT% (big-time throws),
  TWP% (turnover-worthy plays), OFF-SCR (off-script), TTS, CPOE — a
  multi-input composite QB metric.
- Percentile-view efficiency×volume matrix (@statyxio, via @Kaz_cbk):
  EPA/DB vs Sack % scatter in percentile space with value/volume
  quadrants (qualification: 33 dropbacks).
- Statyx defensive-strength tags + SAFETY LOOK MATCHUP: a QB stat
  paired against what the upcoming defense allows (Strong/Elite +
  defensive rank); QB splits vs single-high / two-high shells paired
  with opponent allowed rates and defensive rank — coverage-shell
  matchup analytics (@statyxio).
- Implied-points-exceeded rate (@fball_insights, via
  @ScottBarrettDFB): starts in which the QB's team exceeded its
  pregame implied point total (Penix 11 of 14, 79%) — a market-implied
  QB performance measure.
- Yards-before/after-contact per designed run split: BUF backs most
  before contact (2.80), ATL backs most after (4.34), KC top 3 in
  both — a line-vs-back separation read (@SumerSports).
- Sacks-allowed team extremes: SF 0 (fewest), TB 16 (most) through
  Week 4 (@GridironInfo_).
- Week-4-only / Weeks-3-4-only framing: ATL +0.37 EPA/play weeks 3-4
  (best), PHI -0.29 (last) (@GridironInfo_); points per red zone trip
  ATL 6.30 / CHI 3.78 (@GridironInfo_); Emanuel Wilson backfield share
  W1 8% → W4 76% (@statyxio).

### INNOVATION KERNELS (attributed notes, not build orders)

- Downfield-only QB efficiency: EPA/play + CPOE restricted to
throws of 15+ air yards with a WP 10-90% garbage-time filter, min
10 attempts (@ghatz_28, nflfastR).
- Scramble EPA with scramble counts as a distinct QB rushing-value
layer; Maye leads (~+16.5 EPA, count disputed) (@PattonAnalytics,
StatRankings).
- EPA per dropback crossed with under-center rate as a play-design
fingerprint; Burrow the extreme (~10.5% under-center)
(@PattonAnalytics, StatRankings).
- Play-caller sequencing predictability vs volatility, volatility
defined as the standard deviation of drive-to-drive
predictability (@PattonAnalytics, StatRankings).
- Sacks-taken vs time-to-throw scatter as a QB hold-the-ball
diagnostic (Hurts 12 sacks / 3.21s TTT) (@DynatyzeFF).
- Rest-of-season positional SOS as average opponent rank in 2026
points allowed, playoffs-weighted presentation (@DynatyzeFF,
Matchup Lab).
- FPOE/G (fantasy points over expected per game) as a luck-adjusted
fantasy efficiency layer; XFPTS/G alongside (@DynatyzeFF).
- Catchable air yards with weekly splits as a QB-volume
consistency signal (Stroud 2nd, 979) (@FantasyPtsData).
- Kalshi daily award-odds series as a market-consensus tracking
layer (MVP, CPOY, Protector, Coach, OROY/DROY, OPOY/DPOY)
(@GridironInfo_, Kalshi).
- CPOE x EPA/play quadrant scatter framed as a QB efficiency
frontier (@StartSitEmFF, data @DynatyzeFF).
